niche.habitat: Mid-ring lanes, 1.4–1.8 R_V; avoids chaotic Kessler zones. Also, in the council's sketch (no such creature in this world yet): Kessler Drifter, astroluma avoids saturated Kessler lanes where Drifters graze debris; Drifters trigger cascades that scatter Astroluma's phasing windows. Also, in the council's sketch (no such creature in this world yet): Coth Plume Moth, astroluma's shed ice clumps, rich in radiolytic organics, fall toward Coth and feed Plume Moths on their descent.
niche.diet: Water ice, hydrogen peroxide frost, silicate-organic dust

body: Bilateral body with a foldable, mirror-polished sail membrane; sublimation nozzles; ammonia-brine core encased in electrostatic ice clump armor

chains.trait: Broad silver sail catches starlight and thrusts outward
links: Radiation pressure (9 uPa) exerts continuous thrust
Thrust offsets drag and sublimation mass loss
No reaction mass needed for station-keeping; spirals outward

skill.effect: The creature unfurls its broad silver sail to catch starlight, pushing itself upward and steadying its course against inward pull.

chains.weakness: Eclipse Drift: In Verrin's shadow, thrust vanishes and orbital decay accelerates.
observe: Sail glints like a mirror at low sun angles
Spirals outward steadily without ejecting mass
Drops altitude rapidly when entering planet shadow

journal.en: It rides the star's push like a kite, paying no fuel for the sky.

plausibility.summary: Keep the sail and the eclipse weakness, but pitch the membrane so part of the push is tangential and describe shadow as slow inward drift plus lost photosynthesis, not a fast fall. Delete the '50 m altitude' stat: game numbers are not yours; 'gains height / reduces inward drift' suffices.
fixes: Keep the sail and the eclipse weakness, but pitch the membrane so part of the push is tangential and describe shadow as slow inward drift plus lost photosynthesis, not a fast fall. Delete the '50 m altitude' stat: game numbers are not yours; 'gains height / reduces inward drift' suffices.

analogues.organism: Engineering solar sails (IKAROS/JAXA, 2010) use reflecting films for photon thrust; the Saharan silver ant (Cataglyphis) uses mirrored hairs for radiative cooling, not locomotion.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Sublimation nozzles spray steam to brake and phasing
links: Ring lanes have km/s shear; rendezvous needs precise delta-v
Loose gas provides no traction; reaction mass is required
Throws vapor to adjust relative velocity and orbital phase

skill.effect: The creature vents thick clouds of steam from its nozzles, rapidly slowing its approach so it can safely settle into place.

chains.weakness: Fuel Debt: Using ice for thrust consumes food and armor reserves.
observe: Sprays translucent vapor jets when altering course
Grazes ice to refill vapor reserves

journal.en: Every metre per second is bought with a mouthful of ice.

plausibility.summary: No biological change needed. Remove '0.5 m/s' from the skill text and keep 'shed relative speed and dock safely'; let ice spent on thrust genuinely cost grazing and armour.
fixes: No biological change needed. Remove '0.5 m/s' from the skill text and keep 'shed relative speed and dock safely'; let ice spent on thrust genuinely cost grazing and armour.

analogues.organism: Squid jetting water to manoeuvre and bombardier beetles (Brachinus) ejecting a chemically generated spray; in vacuum the true match is a cold-gas/water thruster.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Spore shells bloom as reflective discs to drift and mate
links: Microgravity prevents sedimentation; gametes must be aimed
Budding releases spore encased in hard shell
Shell expands into sail-disc to catch radiation pressure
Drifts on resonant orbit to phase with mates in L-edge swarms

skill.effect: The creature blooms its spore shells into shimmering discs, drifting gently until it finds and bonds with a nearby mate.

chains.weakness: Sail Snag: Spore cannot steer if sail is punctured; drifts uncontrollably.
observe: Pop open hard shell and snap out silver disc
Disc catches light and drifts away on its own
Follows curved path matching orbital phasing

journal.en: The egg is not a cradle, but a sail waiting for the wind.

plausibility.summary: Set mating in the same ring lane (or the outer ring edge) and have both partners release matched-area discs so they arrive at the same phase, with a brief steam-brake puff (F9) for final approach. If you insist on the Ledge rendezvous, make it a rare rocket-assisted dispersal, not sail drift. Delete '10 m range'.
fixes: Set mating in the same ring lane (or the outer ring edge) and have both partners release matched-area discs so they arrive at the same phase, with a brief steam-brake puff (F9) for final approach. analogues.organism: Dandelion (Taraxacum) pappus as a light disc dispersed by a medium, and tardigrade tuns (Jonsson et al. 2008) for vacuum-tolerant spores; neither uses light pressure to navigate, so the mating mechanism remains unverified.

chains.trait: Ice clump armor shields core from radiation and impacts
links: Ring flux delivers 0.5–5 Gy/day; radiation kills metabolism
Ionizing electrons stop within centimetres of water
Core encapsulated in electrostatic ice/silicate clumps
Armor absorbs dose and stops micrometeoroid fragments

skill.effect: The creature thickens its icy exterior into a heavy armor, strongly deflecting blows and shielding its core from harm.

chains.weakness: Overheat: Temperatures above 260 K breach clathrate skin and kill the cell.
observe: Rocky, clumpy exterior gleams in shadow
Absorbs impact without damage to core
Melts and shrinks if exposed to high heat

journal.en: It wears the ring's ice like a tank, hiding the soft truth inside.

plausibility.summary: Make it a thin, layered/Whipple-style ice-silicate crust over the core (centimetres, self-healed from grazed frost), keep the sail membrane thin and unmortared, and limit the claim to small grains - big fragments should still be lethal. Remove '40%'; say 'small impacts glance off'.

body_plan.origin: Ring-adapted descendant of Coth surface grazers lifted by impact ejecta

temperament: Drifting, opportunistic, phasing-obsessed, cautious of shear
secrets: The sail is not passive: it contains bacteriorhodopsin that converts reflected light to chemical energy, supplementing the ice diet.
The spore can modulate albedo to vanish from ground view, but this costs energy and halts outward thrust.
The sail can be folded to become a dark sphere, making the creature invisible to ground observers, but this risks orbital decay.
moments: On the dark side of Coth, as the star sinks behind Verrin's rim, a shell pops. The disc snaps open, silver as a mirror, and catches the dying light. For a minute, it is a second moon, a silver egg drifting on the star's push, until the planet swallows it and the light dies.

journal.en: The night-sky egg: a satellite that breathes ice and rides light.
From the ground it is a moving star; in the ring, a grazer with a sail.
